Definition: from a compound of G1909 and G5092; properly, esteem, i.e. citizenship; used (in the sense of G2008) of a penalty:--punishment.
BiblicalUsage: Epitimía means punishment — the penalty the church imposes, in the sense of a rebuke carried through. It occurs just once, where Paul says the punishment inflicted by many is enough for the man who sinned. The word is discipline with a limit: enough is enough.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe epitimía is the measure of church discipline: the punishment is enough when it brings the man back, not when it breaks him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
